observation.visible_scene: A stationary view of a weathered white-painted brick wall with two stepped brick pillars, a dark blue spray-paint blotch in the middle, dry grass in the foreground and a pale overcast sky. For the first ~0.9 s the wall is static; a small light-colored spherical object then appears intermittently in the upper sky and near the wall's top edge. After that, a violent bright flash erupts at the wall's center, followed by a fireball with radiating sparks, a rapidly expanding white smoke plume, burning fragments arcing to the right and downward, and a small sustained flame at the base of the wall. The camera does not move; wall, pillars, graffiti and grass keep the same positions throughout.
visible_changes: Frames 1-15: no visible motion; wall, graffiti, pillars and grass unchanged.
Frames 16-20: a small pale sphere appears high in the left sky, descends toward the wall top, briefly vanishes, reappears at the wall's top edge, then drops slightly and disappears.
Frame 24-26: an intense white flash floods the center of the frame, washing out the wall and sky, then subsides leaving an orange-lit wall.

Frames 27-41: a bright fireball with upward and rightward sparks develops at the graffiti area; a white smoke plume grows upward and leftward and increasingly obscures the wall; a jet of fire/sparks shoots to the right, a burning fragment arcs from upper-right toward the lower-right, and a small flame burns at the ground at the wall's base.
Overall lighting of the wall shifts from pale white to warm tan and the sky from pale grey to a darker blue-grey as the flash's illumination fades.
The blue graffiti blotch remains present but is partly hidden behind the smoke plume in later frames.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the small sphere was and whether it struck the wall or triggered the flash.
The state of the scene before the sphere appeared and after the last frame (smoke dissipation, damage outcome).
uncertain_details: The abrupt full-frame white flash at t~1.04 s and the simultaneous change in sky/wall coloration could be the onset of the explosion's light or an editing cut; the excerpt alone cannot confirm a smooth continuous transition.
The sphere's trajectory is only intermittently visible (frames 18 and 21-23 show no sphere), so its exact path and whether it is one object or two passes is uncertain.
Whether the darker sky after the flash reflects genuine ambient light change or camera exposure adjustment to the bright fireball is unclear.
